description: Hurricane wind design and impact glazing required for hospitals in North Carolina coastal and CAMA counties
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — COASTAL WIND DESIGN: The proposed {occupancy} is located in a North Carolina coastal county subject to enhanced wind design requirements under 10A NCAC 14C and the North Carolina Building Code. Hospitals in Brunswick, Carteret, Columbus, Craven, Dare, New Hanover, Onslow, Pender, and other CAMA-designated coastal counties are Risk Category IV structures and must be designed for ASCE 7 wind loads applicable to the coastal North Carolina location. The construction documents do not demonstrate compliance with wind-borne debris region requirements; no impact-resistant glazing or approved storm protection system is specified for exterior glazing. This deficiency must be corrected prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Perform a wind design analysis per ASCE 7 (current North Carolina Building Code adopted edition) for the specific site location using Risk Category IV; document the design wind speed from ASCE 7 wind maps and include wind design parameters on the cover sheet.
2. Determine whether the project site is within the wind-borne debris region per the North Carolina Building Code §1609.2 and ASCE 7 §26.12.3; for sites within the debris region, specify impact-resistant glazing products (tested per ASTM E1886/E1996 or ANSI/DASMA 115) for all exterior windows, doors, and skylights.
3. Provide a glazing product schedule on the architectural drawings identifying the tested impact rating, product approval, and installation instructions for all impact-resistant glazing elements in the wind-borne debris zone.
4. Confirm that roof-to-wall and wall-to-foundation connections are designed for ASCE 7 Risk Category IV wind uplift and lateral loads; include uplift connection details and calculations in the structural drawings submitted to NCDHSR.

description: Emergency generator minimum 72-hour on-site fuel supply required for North Carolina hospitals
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER / FUEL SUPPLY (72-HOUR): The electrical specifications and generator design documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not comply with 10A NCAC 14C .0501, which requires a minimum 72-hour on-site fuel supply for emergency generators at North Carolina-licensed hospitals. The submitted specifications indicate a fuel tank capacity providing less than 72 hours of generator operation at full rated load. This requirement exceeds the NFPA 110 minimum and is specific to North Carolina-licensed healthcare facilities. Revise the fuel storage system design to provide the required 72-hour minimum supply and resubmit drawings to NCDHSR for review.
fix_template:
1. Calculate the fuel consumption rate (gallons per hour) for all emergency generators at full rated load; size the on-site fuel storage system to provide a minimum 72-hour fuel supply at that rate and include the fuel demand calculation in the electrical design narrative.
2. Revise the electrical and plumbing drawings to show the new fuel storage tank configuration, secondary containment, fill connections, level monitoring, and fuel transfer pump arrangement; specify tank design per NFPA 30 and NFPA 110 Level 1.
3. Include in the Division 26 electrical specifications for essential electrical systems a reference to 10A NCAC 14C .0501 and NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance; specify automatic transfer switch transfer time not to exceed 10 seconds for life safety branch loads.
4. Coordinate on-site fuel storage with North Carolina Division of Air Quality and DENR above-ground or underground storage tank registration requirements; include tank registration in the project closeout checklist.

description: North Carolina licensed ambulatory surgical facilities require minimum 200 SF clear floor area per operating room
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ASC OPERATING ROOM MINIMUM SIZE: The floor plan for the proposed ambulatory surgical facility does not comply with 10A NCAC 14D .5500, which requires a minimum 200 SF clear floor area per operating room in North Carolina-licensed ambulatory surgical facilities. The clear floor area must be measured from the interior face of finished walls, excluding fixed casework, equipment recesses, column projections, and scrub sink enclosures. The submitted floor plan indicates one or more operating rooms with clear floor areas below the required 200 SF minimum. Provide dimensioned floor plans confirming compliance with this minimum for each OR.
fix_template:
1. Revise the operating room floor plan to provide a minimum 200 SF net clear floor area measured from the interior face of finished walls, excluding fixed casework, equipment alcoves, column projections, and scrub sink enclosures.
2. Provide an enlarged dimensioned plan for each OR annotating the net clear area calculation; confirm that the surgical table, anesthesia zone, instrument back table, and surgical team circulation can be accommodated within the revised layout per FGI 2022 Part 2.
3. Include an OR room schedule listing each room's gross area and net clear area and referencing 10A NCAC 14D .5500 compliance for each room.
4. Verify that HVAC supply and exhaust air quantities, room pressure relationships, and filtration requirements per ASHRAE 170 and NCDHSR standards are maintained in the revised OR layout.

description: Written ICRA required to accompany construction document submittal for projects in or adjacent to occupied licensed healthcare facilities
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL RISK ASSESSMENT: The construction document submittal for the proposed project in or adjacent to the occupied {occupancy} does not include a written Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) as required by 10A NCAC 14C .0501. North Carolina DHSR requires that a completed ICRA accompany the construction document submittal for any project in an occupied licensed healthcare facility. The ICRA must identify the patient risk group and construction activity type, determine the required ICRA class level, and document the infection control measures to be implemented throughout the project. This document has not been included in the current submittal. Provide the required ICRA prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Complete an ICRA matrix with the facility infection preventionist identifying patient risk group (based on proximity to high-risk patient populations) and construction activity type (Class A–D); determine the required ICRA class level and document specific control measures.
2. Prepare a written ICRA report documenting: physical barrier types and locations, negative pressure requirements and monitoring protocols, HEPA vacuum and dustcontrol requirements for all tools, construction traffic routing, and restrictions on working hours relative to patient care activities.
3. Show on the construction documents (phasing plan or ICRA barrier plan) the physical locations of construction barriers, HVAC isolation points, and construction access/egress routes; confirm barriers are shown from finished floor to structural deck above.
4. Include the completed ICRA as an appendix to the NCDHSR construction document submittal; identify the facility infection preventionist responsible for ongoing ICRA compliance monitoring and include their contact information.

description: North Carolina CON required for new hospitals, additional beds, or capital expenditures exceeding NC thresholds; must precede DHSR plan review
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — CERTIFICATE OF NEED (CON): The proposed project for the {occupancy} appears to involve the establishment of a new hospital, addition of licensed inpatient beds, or capital expenditures that require a Certificate of Need (CON) from the NC Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Certificate of Need Section under NC General Statute §131E-175 et seq. CON approval must be obtained before NCDHSR plan review is initiated for qualifying projects. The current submittal does not include a CON approval letter or a DHHS determination confirming the project does not require CON review. Provide this documentation before NCDHSR plan review can proceed.
fix_template:
1. Determine whether the proposed project meets the CON threshold under NC Gen. Stat. §131E-175 by evaluating whether it involves new hospital establishment, addition of licensed beds, or capital expenditures exceeding NC DHHS CON program thresholds.
2. If CON is required, submit a complete CON application to the NC DHHS Certificate of Need Section and obtain a CON approval letter before submitting construction documents to NCDHSR.
3. If the project does not require CON (below threshold, exemption category, or replacement of existing facilities without added beds/services), obtain a written determination from the NC DHHS Certificate of Need Section confirming the exemption and include this determination in the NCDHSR submittal package.
4. Include the CON approval letter or written exemption determination as the first document in the NCDHSR plan review submittal; NCDHSR plan review will not commence for qualifying projects without this documentation.

description: North Carolina Energy Conservation Code compliance and mechanical commissioning required for licensed hospital construction
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ENERGY CODE / COMMISSIONING: The construction documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not include a North Carolina Energy Conservation Code (NCECC, based on ASHRAE 90.1 with NC amendments) compliance certification or a mechanical commissioning plan as required under 10A NCAC 14C and the NCECC. New licensed hospital construction in North Carolina must demonstrate energy code compliance for HVAC, lighting, and building envelope, and mechanical commissioning is required for new hospital HVAC systems. No energy code compliance documentation and no commissioning scope plan or commissioning authority designation have been included in the current submittal. Provide these documents prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Complete and include North Carolina Energy Conservation Code compliance documentation (COMcheck report for envelope and systems, or equivalent NC-approved energy compliance form) for HVAC, lighting, and building envelope systems; confirm compliance with current ASHRAE 90.1 edition as amended by North Carolina.
2. Review and document any NCECC exceptions applicable to 24-hour healthcare occupancies (e.g., lighting power density exceptions, HVAC setback exceptions for infection control areas); include justification for any exceptions applied.
3. Identify an independent commissioning authority (CxA) for the HVAC systems; include a commissioning scope in the specifications covering pre-functional checklists, functional performance testing, air balance verification, and pressure relationship testing for all critical care areas.
4. Submit the final mechanical commissioning report signed by the CxA to NCDHSR as a project closeout document; the report must include air balance results, pressure relationship measurements for critical spaces, temperature/humidity setpoint verification, and a list of resolved deficiencies.

description: NCDHSR plan review submission required with completed application, project description, and estimated construction cost
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW SUBMISSION: The construction document submittal for the proposed {occupancy} is incomplete and does not fully meet the requirements of 10A NCAC 14C .0501. A complete NCDHSR Plan Review Section submittal must include a completed DHSR plan review application, a written project description, an estimated construction cost, and a complete set of construction documents including site plan, architectural floor plans, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection drawings, and technical specifications. The current submittal is missing [required application / project description / estimated construction cost / drawing disciplines]. Resubmit with all required elements.
fix_template:
1. Complete the NC DHSR Health Care Facility Plan Review application form (available from the NCDHSR Plan Review Section) in full, including facility name, license number, county, project scope, and authorized signature from the facility administrator or owner.
2. Prepare a written project description (minimum 1–2 pages) summarizing the scope of work, affected areas, occupancy classification, proposed changes to licensed services or bed count, construction type, and fire protection approach; include the estimated total construction cost.
3. Assemble the complete construction document set: site plan, floor plans at minimum 1/8-inch scale, reflected ceiling plans, sections as needed, HVAC/mechanical plans and schedules, plumbing plans, electrical plans and single-line diagram, fire protection plans, and project specifications.
4. Submit the complete package to the NC DHSR Plan Review Section, 2711 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-2711, with the applicable plan review fee per the DHSR fee schedule; retain the DHSR receipt of submission for permit tracking.

description: Complete automatic fire sprinkler system per NFPA 13 required throughout new NC licensed hospital construction
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — AUTOMATIC FIRE SPRINKLER SYSTEM: The fire protection drawings for the proposed {occupancy} do not demonstrate that a complete automatic fire sprinkler system designed per NFPA 13 is provided throughout the entire new hospital building as required by 10A NCAC 14C and NFPA 101 as adopted in the North Carolina Building Code with NC amendments. All areas of a new North Carolina-licensed hospital must be protected by an automatic sprinkler system, including mechanical and electrical rooms, storage areas, interstitial spaces, and all occupied and unoccupied spaces. The current fire protection drawings show sprinkler coverage omitted from one or more areas. Revise the drawings to provide complete building sprinkler coverage.
fix_template:
1. Revise the fire protection drawings to show complete automatic fire sprinkler coverage throughout all areas of the building per NFPA 13 (NC-adopted edition), including concealed and accessible spaces above ceilings, mechanical rooms, electrical rooms, storage rooms, and all occupied spaces.
2. Provide a hydraulic design summary on the fire protection drawings confirming the design density, area of application, water supply available, and residual pressure at the most remote sprinkler head; reference the public or private water supply source and flow test data.
3. Specify sprinkler system type, pipe material, hanger design, and seismic bracing in Division 21 specifications per NFPA 13; address sprinkler head type in patient care areas (semi-recessed or concealed as appropriate for infection control and anti-ligature requirements in behavioral health areas).
4. Coordinate the fire sprinkler system design with the NCDHSR plan review submission and the local authority having jurisdiction building permit; both approvals are required before commencing fire protection installation.
